text: Beginningless and having an end, prior non-existence is the absence of an effect before its production. Having a beginning and endless, posterior non-existence is the absence of an effect after its destruction. Absolute non-existence, delimited by the relation of concomitance in all three times and by a contradictory, is like the statement, "There is no pot on the ground." Mutual non-existence, delimited by the relation of identity and by a contradictory, is like the statement, "A pot is not a cloth."
